source_constraint: All facts in these evals must be verifiable against docs.sui.io/onchain-finance/deepbook/deepbookv3/deepbook or github.com/MystenLabs/deepbookv3. No third-party blogs, tutorials, or unofficial documentation.

evals.prompt: What is DeepBook V3 and how does it differ from an AMM like Uniswap?
evals.expected_output: An explanation that DeepBook is a CLOB (central limit order book) on Sui, not an AMM. It supports limit and market orders with price-time priority matching, discrete tick/lot sizes, and a full order book of bids and asks.
expectations: The response identifies DeepBook as a central limit order book (CLOB), not an AMM
The response mentions price-time priority matching
The response mentions support for both limit and market orders
The response mentions tick size and lot size as discrete price/quantity increments
The response notes that DeepBook does not include an end-user interface

evals.prompt: Explain the internal architecture of a DeepBook V3 Pool. What are the three main components?
evals.expected_output: A description of the Pool's three components: Book (order storage and matching via BigVector), State (governance, history, accounts), and Vault (asset settlement and DEEP price conversion).
expectations: The response identifies the three components: Book, State, and Vault
The response explains that the Book manages two BigVector structures for bids and asks
The response explains that State contains Governance, History, and Account submodules
The response explains that the Vault handles asset settlement and maintains DeepPrice conversion rates
The response mentions that BigVector uses a B+ tree for efficient order storage

evals.prompt: What are the three integration models for DeepBook V3 and when should I use each one?
evals.expected_output: A comparison of the three integration approaches: Move package for on-chain protocol integration, SDK & PTBs for apps/bots/wallets, and read-only data queries for price/orderbook access.
expectations: The response lists all three models: Move package, SDK & PTBs, and read-only data
The response explains that Move integration is for protocols requiring on-chain logic guarantees
The response explains that SDK/PTBs is for apps, bots, and wallets using TypeScript
The response explains that read-only is for price and order book queries
The response includes the Move dependency format: deepbook = { mvr = "@deepbook/core" }
The response includes the SDK installation: npm install @mysten/deepbook-v3

evals.prompt: What is the role of the DEEP token in DeepBook V3?
evals.expected_output: An explanation that DEEP is used for fee payment (default method), staking for fee discounts, and governance (proposing and voting on pool parameters).
expectations: The response explains DEEP as the default fee payment token
The response mentions that fees can alternatively be paid in the input token at a 25% premium
The response explains that staking DEEP can reduce taker fees
The response explains governance: users can propose and vote on pool parameters
The response mentions whitelisted pools (DEEP/SUI, DEEP/USDC) have 0% fees

evals.prompt: What is the current DeepBook V3 mainnet package ID and what is the SUI/USDC pool ID?
evals.expected_output: The v6 package ID and the SUI/USDC pool object ID from the contract information page.
expectations: The response provides the v6 package ID: 0x337f4f4f6567fcd778d5454f27c16c70e2f274cc6377ea6249ddf491482ef497
The response provides the SUI/USDC pool ID: 0xe05dafb5133bcffb8d59f4e12465dc0e9faeaa05e3e342a08fe135800e3e4407
